r2062.explain: In good years mothers help the smaller sex catch up; in poor years they give the head start to females, the larger sex, concentrating advantage where survival is likeliest. B contradicts the pattern the researchers found. D reverses the poor-year behavior.

r2063.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2063.passage: A city wanted to reduce traffic congestion by charging drivers a fee to enter downtown during rush hour. Before the fee took effect, the city expanded bus service on routes into downtown. Planners reasoned that without the expanded service, many commuters who could not afford the fee would have no practical way to reach their jobs. The planners' reasoning suggests that they believed
choices: buses would cause more congestion downtown than the cars they replaced during rush hour.
most commuters could easily afford the fee and would keep driving downtown anyway.
the fee would be unnecessary once bus service was expanded, since commuters would switch on their own.
a congestion fee would be fairer if commuters had an affordable alternative to driving.
r2063.explain: The planners expanded buses because some commuters couldn't afford the fee and would otherwise have no way to work. That shows concern for providing an affordable alternative. B contradicts their worry, and C misreads the buses as a replacement for the fee rather than a complement.

r2064.sub: What a sample can and cannot show
r2064.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2064.passage: A researcher interviewed 40 novelists who had each published at least five books and found that 33 of them wrote every day, even if only for a few minutes. She was careful not to conclude that daily writing leads to a successful career, since her study included only novelists who had already succeeded. Her caution reflects the possibility that
choices: novelists who write every day tend to publish fewer books than those who write only when inspired.
many writers who wrote daily never published five books and so were left out of her study.
most of the novelists she interviewed did not actually write every day, despite what they reported.
daily writing becomes unnecessary once a novelist has already published several successful books.
r2064.explain: Studying only successful novelists can't show that daily writing leads to success, because unsuccessful daily writers were never counted. B names that gap. C contradicts her finding, and A and D aren't implied.

r2065.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2065.passage: In 1869 the Suez Canal opened, linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas. Before its completion, ships traveling between Britain and India had to sail around the southern tip of Africa, a journey of about 19,000 kilometers. Through the canal, the trip was roughly 11,000 kilometers. British merchants, who at first had been skeptical of the project, became some of the canal's heaviest users within a decade, which suggests that
choices: the savings in distance outweighed whatever doubts the merchants had when the canal first opened.
the canal was built mainly by British engineers, who persuaded merchants to use it.
British merchants shifted their trade away from India after 1869 toward ports in the Red Sea.
the route around Africa became shorter after the canal opened, which reduced merchants' doubts.
r2065.explain: Initially skeptical merchants became heavy users once the route cut about 8,000 kilometers, which suggests the practical savings overcame their doubts. C contradicts heavy use, and B and D aren't supported.

r2066.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2066.passage: A study of a coastal town found that houses built on elevated foundations suffered far less flood damage in a major storm than nearby houses built at ground level. However, the elevated houses were also, on average, twenty years newer and built under stricter building codes requiring stronger walls and roofs. To determine whether elevation alone reduces flood damage, researchers would most need to compare
choices: elevated houses in this town with elevated houses in a nearby town that the storm did not reach.
the total cost of building elevated houses and ground-level houses under the stricter codes.
elevated and ground-level houses that were built at about the same time under the same codes.
flood damage to the elevated houses in this storm with their damage in earlier, weaker storms.
r2066.explain: Age and building codes are confounding factors. To isolate elevation, the comparison should hold those constant while varying only elevation. A varies nothing, and B and D don't separate elevation from the other factors.

r2067.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2067.passage:
The following text is from a novel. Hiroshi has received a letter from his estranged brother.

Hiroshi placed the letter, unopened, on the windowsill, where it stayed through a week of rain. Each morning he moved it a few centimeters to keep it out of the damp, and each evening he moved it back, so that it would catch the last of the light. By Sunday the envelope had been handled more than any letter he had ever answered. Hiroshi's behavior suggests that he
choices: has forgotten that the letter exists and moves it only because it is in his way.
has already decided never to read the letter and is waiting for a chance to throw it away.
is worried that the rain has damaged the letter so badly that it can no longer be read.
values the letter and protects it, even though he is not yet ready to read what it says.
r2067.explain: He protects the letter from damp and keeps it in the light every day, which shows care, yet he leaves it unopened. A contradicts his daily attention. B goes too far: nothing shows a final decision. C misreads his care as concern over damage that hasn't occurred.

r2068.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2068.passage: Several species of frogs in Central America declined sharply in the 1990s. Biologists considered three explanations: habitat loss, pollution, and a fungal disease. The declines occurred even in protected mountain forests far from roads, farms, and factories, and the dead frogs showed skin infections caused by a chytrid fungus. These observations most strongly support the conclusion that
choices: habitat loss was the main cause, since frogs in protected forests had nowhere else to go.
the chytrid fungus is a more likely cause of the declines than habitat loss or pollution.
pollution from distant factories spread into the protected forests and weakened the frogs.
none of the three explanations can account for declines in forests far from roads and farms.
r2068.explain: Declines in protected forests far from roads and factories weigh against habitat loss and pollution, while infected skin points to the fungus. C invents a pathway the text doesn't mention.

r2069.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2069.passage: A survey of a country's workers found that the average commute lengthened from 26 minutes to 29 minutes over a decade. During the same period, the share of workers who worked entirely from home rose from 5% to 18%. Because the survey's average was calculated only from workers who commuted, the lengthening suggests that
choices: people who still commuted were, on average, traveling longer than commuters had a decade earlier.
working from home caused the commutes of the remaining commuters to become longer over the decade.
most workers spent more time commuting than before, including those who worked from home.
the workers who switched to working from home had previously had the shortest commutes in the country.
r2069.explain: The average covers only commuters, so it shows that commuters' trips grew longer on average. C wrongly includes home workers, who don't commute. D is one possible explanation, but the data can't confirm it, and B claims a cause the data can't establish.

r2070.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
r2070.passage: Some plants produce caffeine in their nectar. Caffeine is bitter, and at high doses it deters insects, but the amounts in nectar are too low for bees to taste. In experiments, bees that fed on nectar containing low doses of caffeine were three times as likely to remember the flower's scent a day later. Plants producing caffeinated nectar may therefore benefit because
choices: the caffeine discourages bees from visiting the plants too often and taking too much nectar.
bees can taste the small amount of caffeine and prefer nectar with a slightly bitter flavor.
bees that remember a plant's scent are more likely to return to that plant and carry its pollen.
the caffeine protects the nectar from spoiling, so bees find it fresh when they arrive.
r2070.explain: The experiment shows improved memory for the flower's scent; a remembered flower is more likely to be revisited and pollinated. A applies to high doses, not the low doses in nectar, and B contradicts "too low for bees to taste."

r3001.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3001.passage: The Atacama Desert receives almost no rain in most some of its weather stations have never recorded measurable rainfall at all.
choices: years, in fact,
years in fact
years; in fact,
years, in fact
r3001.explain: Both sides are independent clauses, and "in fact" is a transition, not a conjunction, so commas alone can't join the clauses. Use a semicolon before "in fact" and a comma after it. A and D are comma splices; B fuses the clauses.

r3002.sub: No comma after a title before a name
r3002.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3002.passage: In 1922, Danish physicist Niels won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his model of the structure of atoms.
choices: Bohr,
Bohr
Bohr—
Bohr;
r3002.explain: "Danish physicist Niels Bohr" is the subject, and nothing should separate a subject from its verb ("won"). A title such as "Danish physicist" placed directly before a name takes no comma either. A, C, and D each put punctuation between the subject and the verb.

r3003.sub: No punctuation inside a long subject-verb unit
r3003.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3003.passage: The tiny pores on the underside of a leaf that open and close to control the exchange of gases called stomata.
choices: are,
are:
are;
are
r3003.explain: The long subject ("The tiny pores … gases") is followed directly by its verb phrase "are called." Nothing should interrupt "are called." A, B, and C each split the verb from its completion.

r3004.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3004.passage: Historian Mónica Ruiz exposed the forged letters by noticing one unremarkable the postage stamps on them had not been issued until two years after the dates written at the top.
choices: detail:
detail,
detail
detail, which
r3004.explain: Both sides are independent clauses, and the second explains what the detail was, so a colon fits. B is a comma splice, C fuses the clauses, and D creates a relative clause ("which the postage stamps … had not been issued") that doesn't make sense.

r3005.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3005.passage: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault—a facility built into a mountain on a remote Norwegian stores duplicate samples of seeds from gene banks around the world.
choices: island—
island,
island;
island
r3005.explain: The interruption opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash. That returns the reader to the main clause: "The Svalbard Global Seed Vault … stores duplicate samples." Mixing a dash and a comma (B) is not standard, and D leaves the interruption open.

r3006.sub: Splice hidden behind a relative clause
r3006.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3006.passage: The first sound recordings were made on cylinders coated with tinfoil, which wore out after only a few by the late 1880s, wax cylinders that could be played dozens of times had replaced them.
choices: playings,
playings
playings, which
playings;
r3006.explain: "The first sound recordings … a few playings" is an independent clause, and so is "by the late 1880s, wax cylinders … had replaced them." A semicolon joins them. The comma before "which" earlier in the sentence can make A look natural, but it creates a comma splice. B fuses the clauses, and C makes no grammatical sense.

r3007.sub: Semicolons in a list with internal commas
r3007.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3007.passage: The expedition set up its three base camps in Lhasa, Kathmandu, Nepal; and Darjeeling, India.
choices: Tibet,
Tibet:
Tibet;
Tibet
r3007.explain: Each list item contains a comma ("Lhasa, Tibet"), so the items are separated by semicolons, as the rest of the sentence already shows ("Nepal; and"). Only a semicolon keeps the list consistent.

r3008.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3008.passage: The question that guided ornithologist Peter Laine's thirty years of fieldwork was deceptively simple: why do some songbirds keep learning new songs throughout their
choices: lives.
lives?
lives?.
lives;
r3008.explain: After the colon, the sentence asks a direct question ("why do some songbirds keep learning…"), so it ends with a question mark. A would be right for an indirect question ("asked why some songbirds keep learning"), but this question is direct. C doubles the end punctuation.

r3009.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3009.passage: Although the comet will not pass near Earth again for another 2,000 astronomers have already calculated its path with remarkable precision.
choices: years;
years,
years.
years:
r3009.explain: "Although … 2,000 years" is a dependent clause, so it can't stand alone or be followed by a semicolon, period, or colon. A comma connects it to the main clause.

r3010.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3010.passage: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest structure built by living organisms it stretches more than 2,300 kilometers along the northeastern coast of Australia.
choices: organisms,
organisms
organisms;
organisms, which
r3010.explain: Each side is an independent clause, so a semicolon is needed. A is a comma splice and B fuses the clauses. D produces "which it stretches," which repeats the subject.

r3011.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3011.passage: Most visitors praised the museum's new wing for its dramatic views of the harbor. Its have drawn criticism from curators, who say the lighting is too dim for viewing paintings.
choices: galleries; however,
galleries however
galleries, however;
galleries, however,
r3011.explain: "However" interrupts a single clause ("Its galleries have drawn criticism"), so it is set off by a pair of commas. A and C put a semicolon inside the clause, splitting the subject from its verb. B leaves the interrupter unpunctuated.

r3012.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3012.passage: In her 2019 study, sociologist Erin Park commuters who walked or biked to work reported higher job satisfaction than those who drove.
choices: found that
found, that
found: that
found; that
r3012.explain: "That commuters … drove" is the object of "found," and nothing should separate a verb from its object. B, C, and D each insert punctuation between them.

r3013.sub: Comma before a conjunction joining clauses
r3013.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3013.passage: The city's first subway line opened in the trains were so crowded during the first week that the operator added extra cars within a month.
r3013.explain: Two independent clauses joined by "and" take a comma before the conjunction. The SAT treats a semicolon before a coordinating conjunction (A) as an error. B and D misplace or add a comma after "and."

r3014.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3014.passage: Some desert plants, such as the barrel cactus and the store water in their stems and can survive months without rain.
choices: saguaro
saguaro;
saguaro—
saguaro,
r3014.explain: The example phrase opens with a comma after "plants," so it closes with a comma after "saguaro," returning to "Some desert plants … store water." C closes with a dash, which doesn't match, and A leaves the phrase open.

r3015.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3015.passage: Having spent a decade cataloging the island's the botanist was startled to find a species she had never seen before.
choices: orchids,
orchids;
orchids.
orchids:
r3015.explain: "Having spent … orchids" is an introductory phrase, not a clause, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon, period, or colon would leave the phrase stranded as a fragment.

r3016.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3016.passage: Red dwarf stars are too faint to be seen from Earth without a they make up roughly three-quarters of the stars in the Milky Way.
choices: telescope, nevertheless,
telescope; nevertheless,
telescope, nevertheless
telescope nevertheless,
r3016.explain: Two independent clauses are joined with a transition, so the transition takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it. A and C are comma splices, and D fuses the clauses.

r3017.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3017.passage: The kit contained everything a field researcher would a GPS unit, a soil probe, sample bags, and a waterproof notebook.
choices: need:
need;
need
need, including:
r3017.explain: The clause before the blank is complete, and a list follows, so a colon is correct. A semicolon (B) must be followed by an independent clause. D places a colon after "including," which leaves an incomplete phrase before the colon.

r3018.sub: Semicolon between clauses with a conditional
r3018.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3018.passage: The bridge's main cables are made of thousands of steel wires bundled one wire breaks, the others share its load.
choices: together, if
together if
together; if
together, which if
r3018.explain: "The bridge's main cables … bundled together" is a complete clause, and so is "if one wire breaks, the others share its load." A semicolon joins them. A is a comma splice. B attaches "if one wire breaks" to "bundled together," which changes the meaning and leaves "the others share its load" stranded.

r3019.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3019.passage: Ada Lovelace, the daughter of the poet Lord is often described as the first computer programmer.
choices: Byron
Byron;
Byron—
Byron,
r3019.explain: The appositive "the daughter of the poet Lord Byron" opens with a comma, so it must close with one before the verb "is." C mismatches the punctuation, and A leaves the appositive open.

r3020.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3020.passage: Bees visit only one type of flower on each foraging trip are especially effective pollinators.
choices: , which
that
, that
that,
r3020.explain: The clause identifies which bees are effective pollinators, so it is essential and takes no commas: "Bees that visit … are especially effective pollinators." A would make the clause nonessential and claim that all bees visit only one type of flower.

r3021.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3021.passage: Scholars had studied the medieval manuscript for more than a no one noticed the faint drawings in its margins until it was photographed under ultraviolet light.
choices: century; yet
century, yet
century yet
century, yet,
r3021.explain: "Yet" is a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses, so it takes a comma before it. A semicolon before a conjunction (A) is treated as an error, and nothing should follow "yet."

r3022.sub: Indirect question ends like a statement
r3022.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3022.passage: Biologists have long debated how salmon find the streams where they some suspect that the fish follow the scent of their home waters.
choices: hatched;
hatched?
hatched,
hatched
r3022.explain: "Biologists have long debated how salmon find the streams where they hatched" is a statement that contains an indirect question, so it takes no question mark. It is an independent clause, as is "some suspect…," so a semicolon joins them. C is a comma splice, and D fuses the clauses.

r3023.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3023.passage: The aye-aye—a lemur that taps on tree bark and listens for the echoes of hidden insect is found only on Madagascar.
choices: larvae,
larvae;
larvae
larvae—
r3023.explain: The interruption begins with a dash after "aye-aye," so it must end with a dash before the verb "is." The length of the interruption makes it easy to lose track of how it began.

r3024.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3024.passage: Throughout the long winter months at the research station in the scientists kept a daily log of the sea ice's thickness.
choices: Antarctica;
Antarctica:
Antarctica,
Antarctica.
r3024.explain: "Throughout … in Antarctica" is an introductory phrase, not a clause. It can't be followed by a semicolon, colon, or period, which would leave it as a fragment. A comma joins it to the main clause.

r3025.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3025.passage: The ancient Greek mathematician calculated the circumference of Earth with surprising accuracy by comparing the angles of shadows in two cities.
choices: Eratosthenes,
Eratosthenes
, Eratosthenes,
Eratosthenes—
r3025.explain: The name identifies which mathematician is meant, so it is essential and takes no commas, and nothing should come between the subject and its verb "calculated." C treats the name as optional, but the sentence needs it.

r3026.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3026.passage: The new vaccine must be stored at temperatures below hospitals without ultracold freezers cannot use it.
choices: −70°C, therefore,
−70°C therefore,
−70°C; therefore,
−70°C, therefore
r3026.explain: Two independent clauses joined by the transition "therefore" need a semicolon before the transition and a comma after it. A and D are comma splices; B fuses the clauses.

r3027.sub: Semicolons in a list of names with descriptions
r3027.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3027.passage: The festival's lineup featured Ana Tijoux, a Chilean rapper; Bomba Estéreo, a Colombian and Rodrigo y Gabriela, a Mexican guitar duo.
choices: band;
band,
band:
band
r3027.explain: Each item already contains a comma ("Ana Tijoux, a Chilean rapper"), so semicolons separate the items, as the sentence does after "rapper." A comma (B) would blur where one item ends and the next begins.

r3028.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3028.passage: The first trial of the drug produced no measurable effect. the second trial, which used a higher dose, reduced symptoms in most participants.
choices: However
However;
However:
However,
r3028.explain: An introductory transition is followed by a comma. A semicolon or colon after "However" would separate it from the clause it introduces, and no punctuation at all leaves the transition running into the clause.

r3029.sub: Colon before a quotation that explains
r3029.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3029.passage: The sign at the trailhead gave hikers a single piece of “Stay on the marked path.”
choices: advice;
advice:
advice that
advice, which
r3029.explain: The clause before the blank is complete, and the quotation spells out what the advice was, so a colon introduces it. A semicolon (A) needs an independent clause after it. C and D turn the quotation into a broken relative clause.

r3030.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3030.passage: A former engineer who designed bridges for three Teresa Okoye now builds furniture from reclaimed timber.
choices: decades
decades;
decades,
decades:
r3030.explain: "A former engineer … three decades" is an introductory phrase describing Teresa Okoye, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. Without the comma, the phrase runs into her name.

r3031.sub: Agreement with a distant singular subject
r3031.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3031.passage: The collection of letters written by the explorer to her sisters during her three voyages to the Arctic now held at the national archive in Oslo.
choices: are
were
is
have been
r3031.explain: The subject is "collection," which is singular; "letters," "sisters," and "voyages" are inside modifying phrases. "Now" calls for the present tense: "is." A and D are plural, and B is plural and past.

r3032.sub: Inverted sentence with a compound subject
r3032.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3032.passage: Among the artifacts recovered from the sixteenth-century shipwreck a bronze astrolabe and a set of brass navigational dividers.
choices: were
was
is
has been
r3032.explain: In an inverted sentence the subject comes after the verb: "a bronze astrolabe and a set of … dividers," a compound (plural) subject. "Recovered" places the event in the past, so "were" is correct. B, C, and D are singular; "artifacts" is not the subject.

r3033.sub: Collective noun takes a singular pronoun
r3033.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3033.passage: After two years of hearings, the city's transportation committee released final report, which recommended extending light-rail service to the airport.
choices: their
its
it's
they're
r3033.explain: "Committee" is a single body, so the possessive pronoun is "its." A is plural; C means "it is" and D means "they are."

r3034.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3034.passage: For decades, the three findings on lake sediments were scattered across a dozen journals; in 2021 they were finally collected in a single volume.
choices: researcher's
researchers
researchers's
researchers'
r3034.explain: The findings belong to three researchers, so the plural possessive "researchers'" is needed. A is singular possessive, B is plural with no possession, and C isn't a standard form.

r3035.sub: A finite verb after a long subject
r3035.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3035.passage: Harriet Tubman, who escaped slavery in 1849 and later guided dozens of others to freedom along the network of safe houses known as the Underground Railroad, as a scout and spy for the Union Army during the Civil War.
choices: serving
served
having served
to serve
r3035.explain: Strip the clause between the commas and the sentence reads "Harriet Tubman as a scout and spy." It still needs a main verb, and only "served" is one. A, C, and D are verb forms that can't serve as a sentence's main verb.

r3036.sub: Past tense in a past narrative
r3036.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3036.passage: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold had killed the bacteria growing in one of his laboratory dishes. He soon the substance produced by the mold "penicillin."
choices: names
will name
named
is naming
r3036.explain: The passage narrates past events ("In 1928," "noticed," "had killed"), so the simple past "named" keeps the tense consistent.

r3037.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3037.passage: Using a technique called radiocarbon dating,
choices: the bones were found by researchers to be about 9,000 years old.
the age of the bones was determined to be about 9,000 years.
it was determined that the bones were about 9,000 years old.
researchers determined that the bones were about 9,000 years old.
r3037.explain: The opening phrase describes someone using a technique, so the subject right after the comma must be the people who used it: "researchers." In A and B, the phrase seems to describe the bones or their age using the technique, and in C the subject "it" names no one.

r3038.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3038.passage: Each of the more than thirty paintings in Claude Monet's series of Rouen Cathedral the building's facade at a different time of day.
choices: depicts
depict
are depicting
have depicted
r3038.explain: The subject is "Each," which is singular; "paintings" is part of the phrase "of the more than thirty paintings." Only "depicts" is singular. The present tense fits a description of artworks.

r3039.sub: "Neither … nor" agrees with the nearer subject
r3039.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3039.passage: Neither the study's lead author nor her two coauthors able to explain why the bacteria stopped dividing after the third day.
choices: were
was
is
has been
r3039.explain: With "neither … nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "her two coauthors," which is plural. The passage describes a completed study, so the past tense "were" fits. B, C, and D are singular.

r3040.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3040.passage: The volunteer program trains residents to identify invasive plants, them from city parks, and replant the cleared areas with native species.
choices: removing
removed
to be removing
remove
r3040.explain: The series follows "to": "to identify …, remove …, and replant …." The middle item must match the base forms "identify" and "replant." The other choices break the parallel structure.

r3041.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3041.passage: Studying the songs of humpback whales over several decades researchers trace how musical patterns spread from one population to another across the Pacific.
choices: have helped
has helped
helping
to help
r3041.explain: The subject is the gerund phrase "Studying the songs …," which is singular even though it contains the plural nouns "songs," "whales," and "decades." "Has helped" agrees and serves as the main verb. C and D aren't finite verbs.

r3042.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3042.passage: One of the oldest known maps of the night sky painted on the ceiling of an Egyptian tomb more than 3,000 years ago.
choices: were
are
was
have been
r3042.explain: The subject is "One," not "maps" or "sky." It's singular, and "more than 3,000 years ago" calls for the past tense: "was."

r3043.sub: Verb in a relative clause matches its antecedent
r3043.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3043.passage: The solar particles that the northern lights travel from the Sun to Earth in about two to three days.
choices: causes
is causing
has caused
cause
r3043.explain: "That" refers to "particles," which is plural, so the verb in the relative clause is "cause." The general fact calls for the present tense. A, B, and C are singular forms.

r3044.sub: Past perfect for an earlier past action
r3044.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3044.passage: By the time the rescue team reached the stranded climbers on the morning of June 14, the climbers on the ledge for nearly two days.
choices: have been waiting
had been waiting
are waiting
will have waited
r3044.explain: The waiting happened before another past event (the team's arrival), so the past perfect progressive "had been waiting" is correct. A is present perfect, which links to the present, not to a past moment.

r3045.sub: Plural pronoun for a plural noun
r3045.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3045.passage: Hummingbirds can hover in place because they rotate wings in a figure-eight pattern, generating lift on both the forward and backward strokes.
choices: its
it's
their
they're
r3045.explain: The pronoun refers to "Hummingbirds," which is plural, so "their" is correct. B and D are contractions.

r3046.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3046.passage: The library's new reading room for young readers was designed with input from local students, and several of the suggestions, including a window seat and a reading nook, appear in the final plans.
choices: children's
childrens'
childrens
children
r3046.explain: "Children" is already plural, so its possessive adds an apostrophe and s: "children's." "Childrens" isn't a word in standard English, so B and C fail, and D lacks possession.

r3047.sub: "As well as" doesn't make a plural subject
r3047.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3047.passage: The quartet's first violinist, as well as the two cellists who joined the group last year, at the national conservatory in Vienna.
choices: were trained
have trained
was trained
are training
r3047.explain: "As well as the two cellists…" is a phrase set off by commas; it doesn't make the subject plural. The subject is "first violinist," so the singular "was trained" is correct. The other choices are plural.

r3048.sub: Plural subject with a long prepositional phrase
r3048.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3048.passage: The effects of the three-year drought on the region's wheat harvest more severe than agricultural economists had predicted.
choices: were
was
is
has been
r3048.explain: The subject is "effects," which is plural; "drought" and "harvest" are inside prepositional phrases. "Had predicted" places the comparison in the past, so "were" is correct.

r3049.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3049.passage: The poet Ocean Vuong, first collection won the T.S. Eliot Prize, has also written a widely praised novel.
choices: who's
whose
who
whom
r3049.explain: The blank needs a possessive (the first collection belongs to the poet): "whose." A means "who is," which doesn't fit, and C and D aren't possessive.

r3050.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3050.passage: The study identified several genes that how well wheat plants tolerate drought, raising hopes for more resilient varieties.
choices: influences
influencing
to influence
influence
r3050.explain: "That" refers to "genes," which is plural, and the relative clause needs a finite verb: "influence." A is singular, and B and C aren't finite.

r3051.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3051.passage: The size and shape of a finch's beak closely to the kind of food the bird eats, a relationship Charles Darwin noticed in the Galápagos Islands.
choices: corresponds
is corresponding
correspond
has corresponded
r3051.explain: "The size and shape" is a compound subject joined by "and," so it's plural: "correspond." "Beak" is part of a prepositional phrase, which makes the singular forms tempting.

r3052.sub: "The number of" takes a singular verb
r3052.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3052.passage: According to the park's annual surveys, the number of bird species recorded in the wetland nearly doubled since the restoration project began in 1998.
choices: have
has
are
were
r3052.explain: "The number" is singular; "species" belongs to the phrase "of bird species." "Since … 1998" calls for the present perfect: "has … doubled." A is plural; C and D don't form a correct verb with "doubled" here.

r3053.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3053.passage: The vaquita, a small porpoise found only in the northern Gulf of California, is critically endangered, and population has fallen to roughly ten animals.
choices: its
their
it's
they're
r3053.explain: The pronoun refers to "The vaquita," which is singular, and the blank needs a possessive: "its." C means "it is." B is plural.

r3054.sub: A series takes a singular verb
r3054.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3054.passage: A series of experiments conducted at three universities that the compound slows the growth of certain tumors in mice.
choices: have shown
showing
are showing
has shown
r3054.explain: The subject is "series," which is singular; "experiments" and "universities" are inside modifying phrases. "Has shown" agrees. B isn't a finite verb.

r3055.sub: Modifier must touch what it modifies
r3055.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3055.passage: Founded in 1636 as a school for training ministers,
choices: Harvard's original curriculum emphasized Latin, Greek, and theology.
Latin, Greek, and theology were emphasized in Harvard's original curriculum.
the emphasis of Harvard's original curriculum was on Latin, Greek, and theology.
Harvard originally emphasized Latin, Greek, and theology in its curriculum.
r3055.explain: The opening phrase describes something that was founded in 1636: Harvard. Only D puts "Harvard" right after the comma. A makes the curriculum the thing founded, and B and C make the subjects or the emphasis the thing founded.

r3056.sub: Present tense for a current state
r3056.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3056.passage: The Rosetta Stone, which was discovered in Egypt in 1799, on display at the British Museum in London, where millions of visitors see it each year.
choices: is
was
had been
will be
r3056.explain: The main clause describes the stone's current state, as "see it each year" shows, so the present tense "is" is correct. The past tense belongs to the relative clause about its discovery.

r3057.sub: Subject-verb agreement after a quoted title
r3057.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3057.passage: Hidden Figures, a book about the Black women mathematicians whose calculations helped launch the first American astronauts into orbit, adapted into a film in 2016.
choices: were
was
have been
are
r3057.explain: The subject is the book title, a single work, so the verb is singular even though the title and the appositive contain plural words ("Figures," "mathematicians," "astronauts"). "In 2016" calls for the past: "was."

r3058.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3058.passage: Marie Curie and her daughter Irène Joliot-Curie are the only mother and daughter to have each won a Nobel Prize, and research on radioactivity laid the groundwork for nuclear medicine.
choices: her
its
their
one's
r3058.explain: The pronoun refers to both women, a plural antecedent, so "their" is correct. A would refer to only one of them, and B and D don't fit people at all.

r3059.sub: Finite verb in a sentence with an appositive and a clause
r3059.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3059.passage: The axolotl, a salamander that can regrow lost limbs, parts of its heart, and even sections of its brain, in the wild only in a few canals and lakes near Mexico City.
choices: survives
surviving
having survived
to survive
r3059.explain: After the long appositive, the sentence still needs a main verb for "The axolotl." Only "survives" is a finite verb, and it agrees with the singular subject. The present tense fits a current fact.

r3060.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
r3060.passage: In the archive's oldest box of records, there a ship's log, three letters from the captain, and a hand-drawn map of the harbor.
choices: is
was
are
has been
r3060.explain: In a "there" sentence, the verb agrees with what follows: "a ship's log, three letters …, and a hand-drawn map," a compound (plural) subject. The present tense matches a description of what the box contains now, so "are" is correct.

r4001.sub: A difference on one specific dimension
r4001.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the atmospheres of Venus and Earth. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4001.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Venus and Earth are similar in size and mass.
  • Venus's atmosphere is about 96% carbon dioxide.
  • Earth's atmosphere is about 0.04% carbon dioxide.
  • The surface pressure on Venus is about 92 times that on Earth.
  • Both planets have volcanoes.
choices: Whereas carbon dioxide makes up about 96% of Venus's atmosphere, it makes up only about 0.04% of Earth's.
Venus and Earth, unlike many other planets, are similar in size and mass, and both have volcanoes.
Although Venus and Earth both have volcanoes, Venus is also similar to Earth in size and in mass.
Like Earth's atmosphere, Venus's atmosphere contains carbon dioxide, and both planets have volcanoes.
r4001.explain: The goal names two things: a difference and atmospheres. A contrasts carbon dioxide levels in the two atmospheres. B uses "unlike" but describes a similarity between the two planets, C uses "Although" but lists only similarities, and D mentions the atmospheres only to say what they share.

r4002.sub: Aim and method of a study
r4002.stem: The student wants to present the study's aim and its methodology. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4002.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • In 2022, ecologist Liang Wei studied urban foxes in London.
  • She wanted to know whether city foxes are bolder than rural foxes.
  • She placed unfamiliar objects near food in 30 urban and 30 rural fox territories.
  • Urban foxes were more likely to approach and touch the objects.
  • Rural foxes more often avoided the food altogether.
choices: Liang Wei found that urban foxes in London were more likely than rural foxes to approach and touch unfamiliar objects.
In 2022, ecologist Liang Wei studied urban foxes in London, finding that they were bolder than rural foxes.
Rural foxes often avoided food placed near unfamiliar objects, while urban foxes approached the objects, Liang Wei found.
To learn whether city foxes are bolder, Liang Wei put unfamiliar objects near food in 30 urban and 30 rural territories.
r4002.explain: The goal has two parts: the aim (whether city foxes are bolder) and the method (objects placed near food in 60 territories). D gives both. A, B, and C report results instead.

r4003.sub: Introducing a work to an unfamiliar audience
r4003.stem: The student wants to introduce the novel to an audience unfamiliar with Achebe. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4003.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Things Fall Apart is a novel by Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe.
  • It was published in 1958.
  • It follows Okonkwo, a leader in an Igbo village, as British colonizers and missionaries arrive.
  • It has been translated into more than 50 languages.
  • Achebe later wrote four more novels.
choices: Chinua Achebe, who later wrote four more novels, published Things Fall Apart in 1958.
Things Fall Apart, a 1958 novel by Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe, follows an Igbo leader as colonizers arrive.
Translated into more than 50 languages, Things Fall Apart follows Okonkwo as British missionaries arrive.
Okonkwo, a leader in an Igbo village, is the main character of Achebe's 1958 novel Things Fall Apart.
r4003.explain: An audience unfamiliar with Achebe needs to know who he is and what the novel is about. B identifies Achebe as a Nigerian writer and summarizes the story. A names Achebe without saying who he is or what the novel is about, C never mentions Achebe, and D names him without identifying him.

r4004.sub: An advantage relative to an alternative
r4004.stem: The student wants to highlight an advantage of perovskite panels over silicon panels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4004.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Most solar panels are made with silicon.
  • Perovskite is a crystal structure that can also convert sunlight into electricity.
  • Perovskite panels can be made at lower temperatures than silicon panels, which reduces manufacturing costs.
  • Perovskite panels currently degrade faster than silicon panels when exposed to moisture.
  • Researchers are testing protective coatings for perovskite.
choices: Perovskite panels currently degrade faster than silicon panels when exposed to moisture, researchers have found.
Like silicon panels, perovskite panels convert sunlight into electricity, and researchers are testing coatings for them.
Perovskite panels can be made at lower temperatures than silicon ones, which cuts manufacturing costs.
Researchers are testing coatings that could protect perovskite panels from the moisture that degrades them.
r4004.explain: The goal is an advantage over silicon. C compares manufacturing temperature and cost, favoring perovskite. A is a disadvantage, B is a similarity, and D describes ongoing research rather than an advantage.

r4005.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about animal navigation and support it with an example. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4005.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Many animals use Earth's magnetic field to navigate.
  • Loggerhead sea turtles return to the beach where they hatched, sometimes after decades at sea.
  • Experiments suggest that the turtles recognize the magnetic "signature" of their home coastline.
  • European robins can sense magnetic direction using proteins in their eyes.
  • The mechanism behind magnetic sensing is still debated.
choices: Many animals navigate by Earth's magnetic field; loggerhead turtles, for example, find home by its signature.
Loggerhead sea turtles return to the beach where they hatched, sometimes after spending decades at sea.
The mechanism that allows animals such as loggerhead turtles to sense magnetic fields is still debated.
European robins sense magnetic direction with eye proteins, and loggerhead turtles return to their home beaches.
r4005.explain: A states the generalization ("Many animals navigate by Earth's magnetic field") and then gives the turtles as an example of it. B gives the example without the generalization. C concerns an open question rather than a generalization, and D lists two facts without stating a general claim or connecting them.

r4006.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Anning and Ameghino. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4006.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Mary Anning (1799–1847) was an English fossil collector.
  • She discovered the first correctly identified ichthyosaur skeleton.
  • Because she was a woman, she was excluded from the Geological Society of London.
  • Florentino Ameghino (1854–1911) was an Argentine paleontologist.
  • He had no formal university training but described hundreds of fossil species.
choices: Unlike Ameghino, who was Argentine and lived later, Anning was English and worked in the early 1800s.
Anning, who discovered the first correctly identified ichthyosaur, was excluded from the Geological Society.
Ameghino described hundreds of fossil species, while Anning discovered the first correctly identified ichthyosaur.
Anning and Ameghino both made major contributions to paleontology without the usual credentials of their fields.
r4006.explain: The goal is a similarity. Both made important discoveries while outside the usual credentials: Anning was excluded from the society, Ameghino lacked university training. A and C present differences, and B concerns only Anning.

r4007.stem: The student wants to present the study's main finding and explain why it occurred. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4007.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Researchers tested whether planting strips of wildflowers beside farm fields affects crop pests.
  • They compared 20 fields with wildflower strips and 20 fields without them.
  • Fields with wildflower strips had 40% fewer aphids.
  • The strips attracted ladybugs and hoverflies, which eat aphids.
  • Farmers with strips used less pesticide.
choices: Researchers compared 20 fields with wildflower strips and 20 without them to see how the strips affected crop pests.
Fields with wildflower strips had 40% fewer aphids, likely because the strips drew in aphid-eating insects.
Farmers who planted wildflower strips beside their fields used less pesticide than other farmers did.
Ladybugs and hoverflies, which eat aphids, were attracted to the strips of wildflowers planted beside farm fields.
r4007.explain: The goal pairs the finding (40% fewer aphids) with a reason (the strips drew aphid predators). B gives both. A describes the method, C a consequence, and D a fact without the finding.

r4008.sub: Specific result from a study with several results
r4008.stem: The student wants to emphasize how important library computers are to users without home internet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4008.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A 2023 survey asked 1,200 public library users how they used the library.
  • 64% borrowed print books.
  • 41% used the library's computers or internet access.
  • 23% attended a class or event.
  • Among users without home internet, 78% used library computers.
choices: In a 2023 survey of 1,200 library users, 41% reported using the library's computers or internet access.
Most library users in a 2023 survey (64%) borrowed print books, while 41% used the library's computers.
In a 2023 survey, 78% of library users without home internet said they used library computers.
Nearly a quarter of library users attended a class or event, and 41% used the computers, a 2023 survey found.
r4008.explain: The goal concerns a specific group: users without home internet. Only C reports that group's figure. A gives the rate for all users, which is lower and doesn't address the group.

r4009.sub: Contrast of a claim with new evidence
r4009.stem: The student wants to present the 2020 study's findings as a challenge to the long-standing theory. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4009.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Easter Island's population collapsed before Europeans arrived in 1722, according to a long-standing theory.
  • The theory holds that islanders cut down all the trees, causing ecological disaster.
  • A 2020 study of radiocarbon dates and population records found no evidence of a collapse before 1722.
  • The study suggests that the population remained stable until European contact brought disease and enslavement.
choices: A 2020 study found no evidence for the long-held theory that Easter Island's population collapsed before 1722.
Easter Island's population collapsed before 1722, the theory holds, because islanders cut down all the trees.
Europeans arrived on Easter Island in 1722, bringing disease and enslavement, according to a 2020 study.
A 2020 study of radiocarbon dates and population records examined Easter Island's history before and after 1722.
r4009.explain: The goal requires both the old theory and the study's contrary finding. A names the theory and states that the study found no evidence for it. B restates the theory as fact, C reports what the study suggests without mentioning the theory, and D mentions the study without its finding.

r4010.sub: Explaining a term to a general audience
r4010.stem: The student wants to define biomimicry and give an example. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4010.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • "Biomimicry" is the practice of designing products by imitating structures found in nature.
  • Velcro was inspired by burrs that stuck to an engineer's clothing.
  • The nose of Japan's Shinkansen bullet train was redesigned to resemble a kingfisher's beak.
  • The redesign reduced noise when the train exited tunnels.
  • Biomimicry has been used in architecture, medicine, and robotics.
choices: Biomimicry has been used in architecture, medicine, and robotics, as well as in the design of Velcro.
The nose of Japan's Shinkansen bullet train was redesigned to resemble a kingfisher's beak, reducing tunnel noise.
Both Velcro and the Shinkansen bullet train were inspired by nature, and both were redesigned to reduce noise.
Biomimicry, designing products by imitating nature, gave us Velcro, which was inspired by burrs.
r4010.explain: D defines the term and gives an example (Velcro). A lists uses without defining biomimicry, B offers an example without a definition, and C misstates the notes: only the train was redesigned to reduce noise.

r4011.sub: A cause and its effect over time
r4011.stem: The student wants to explain how a single event in 1859 led to a large-scale environmental problem. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4011.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • In 1859, rabbits were released on a property in Australia for hunting.
  • With few predators, the rabbit population grew rapidly.
  • By the 1920s, an estimated 10 billion rabbits lived in Australia.
  • The rabbits ate native plants and caused soil erosion.
  • A 3,250-kilometer fence was built to try to contain them.
choices: To contain the rabbits that had damaged native plants, Australians built a fence 3,250 kilometers long.
Rabbits released in Australia in 1859, with few predators, grew to about 10 billion and damaged native plants.
By the 1920s, an estimated 10 billion rabbits lived in Australia, where they ate native plants and caused erosion.
Rabbits, which eat native plants and cause soil erosion, have few predators in Australia, where they were released.
r4011.explain: The goal links the 1859 release to a large environmental problem. B traces the chain: release, rapid growth without predators, vast numbers, damage. C gives the scale without the cause, and A describes a response.

r4012.stem: The student wants to emphasize the surprising size of Pando as a single living thing. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4012.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The Pando aspen grove in Utah looks like a forest of about 47,000 trees.
  • All of the trees are genetically identical and share one root system.
  • Pando is therefore considered a single organism.
  • It covers about 43 hectares.
  • Its weight is estimated at about 6,000 metric tons.
choices: Pando, a grove of about 47,000 aspen trees in Utah, covers about 43 hectares of land.
The trees in Pando are genetically identical and share one root system, so Pando is considered a single organism.
Though it looks like a forest, Pando is a single organism covering 43 hectares and weighing about 6,000 tons.
Pando's 47,000 trees are genetically identical, and together they weigh an estimated 6,000 metric tons.
r4012.explain: The goal combines "single living thing" with "surprising size." C explains that the apparent forest is one organism and gives its area and weight. B and D explain the single-organism point without conveying size.

r4013.stem: The student wants to emphasize that movable type existed in Asia long before Gutenberg's press. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4013.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The printing press was developed in Europe by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440.
  • Movable type had been invented much earlier in China, by Bi Sheng, around 1040.
  • Bi Sheng's type was made of baked clay.
  • In Korea, metal movable type was used to print a Buddhist text in 1377.
  • Gutenberg used metal type and an oil-based ink.
choices: Gutenberg used metal type and an oil-based ink, while Bi Sheng's earlier movable type was made of baked clay.
Movable type existed in China by 1040 and metal type in Korea by 1377, long before Gutenberg's press of 1440.
Bi Sheng's movable type, made of baked clay, was invented in China and later improved by Gutenberg.
Johannes Gutenberg developed the printing press in Europe around 1440, using metal type and an oil-based ink.
r4013.explain: The goal requires the Asian dates and the comparison with Gutenberg. B gives both the Chinese (1040) and Korean (1377) dates and places them "long before" 1440. C describes Bi Sheng's type without any timing, and A and D never say which came first.

r4014.sub: An audience already familiar with the topic
r4014.stem: The student wants to tell an audience already familiar with CRISPR about a recent milestone. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4014.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • CRISPR is a tool that lets scientists edit DNA at precise locations.
  • It was adapted from a defense system that bacteria use against viruses.
  • In 2023, a CRISPR-based treatment for sickle cell disease was approved in the United States.
  • The treatment edits a patient's own blood stem cells.
  • It is the first approved medicine that uses CRISPR.
choices: CRISPR, a tool adapted from a bacterial defense system, lets scientists edit DNA at precise locations.
CRISPR was adapted from a defense system that bacteria use against viruses and now edits human blood stem cells.
In 2023, a sickle cell treatment that edits patients' own blood stem cells became the first approved medicine to use CRISPR.
Scientists use CRISPR, a tool for editing DNA at precise locations, to treat diseases such as sickle cell disease.
r4014.explain: An audience familiar with CRISPR doesn't need it explained (A, B, D); what's new to them is the milestone. C reports the 2023 approval and why it is a first.

r4015.sub: A contrast within one group over time
r4015.stem: The student wants to emphasize that U.S. farms produced more even as the farm workforce shrank. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4015.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • In 1900, about 40% of the U.S. workforce worked on farms.
  • By 2000, less than 2% did.
  • Total farm output in the U.S. was far higher in 2000 than in 1900.
  • Tractors, fertilizers, and new crop varieties greatly increased output per worker.
choices: Unlike in 1900, when about 40% of U.S. workers were on farms, tractors were widely used on farms in 2000.
In 1900, about 40% of the U.S. workforce worked on farms, compared with less than 2% in 2000.
Tractors, fertilizers, and new crop varieties greatly increased the output of each U.S. farm worker after 1900.
The share of U.S. workers on farms fell from about 40% to under 2% from 1900 to 2000, yet output rose.
r4015.explain: The goal pairs two trends: the shrinking workforce and the rising output. D contrasts them directly. C explains why productivity rose but doesn't state either trend. A uses "Unlike," but its contrast concerns tractors.

r4016.sub: A quote's context for the reader
r4016.stem: The student wants to present Carson's quotation and explain her influence. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4016.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Rachel Carson was a marine biologist and writer.
  • Her 1962 book Silent Spring documented harm caused by pesticides such as DDT.
  • The book prompted public concern and influenced the U.S. ban on DDT in 1972.
  • In the book, Carson wrote, "In nature nothing exists alone."
choices: Carson, whose Silent Spring helped bring about the U.S. DDT ban, wrote, "In nature nothing exists alone."
Rachel Carson, a marine biologist and writer, published Silent Spring in 1962, ten years before the DDT ban.
Silent Spring (1962) documented the harm caused by pesticides such as DDT and prompted public concern.
"In nature nothing exists alone," wrote Rachel Carson, a marine biologist and writer, in her book Silent Spring.
r4016.explain: Only A includes the quotation and also explains Carson's influence (the book helped lead to the DDT ban).

r4017.stem: The student wants to explain why ground-penetrating radar is useful to archaeologists. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4017.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Archaeologists often cannot excavate every part of a large site.
  • Ground-penetrating radar sends radio waves into the soil.
  • The waves reflect off buried walls and objects, creating a map of what lies underground.
  • The method does not disturb the soil.
  • Archaeologists used it to map an entire Roman town in Italy without digging.
choices: Ground-penetrating radar sends radio waves into the soil, where the waves reflect off buried walls and other objects.
Mapping buried structures without digging, ground-penetrating radar lets archaeologists study sites too large to excavate.
Archaeologists used ground-penetrating radar to map an entire Roman town in Italy in a single project.
By sending radio waves into the soil, ground-penetrating radar creates a detailed map of whatever lies underground.
r4017.explain: The goal is about usefulness. B connects what the method does (maps without digging) to an archaeological need (sites too large to excavate). A and D explain how it works but not why it helps, and C reports one use without saying what made the method valuable there.

r4018.sub: Comparing two quantities with a ratio
r4018.stem: The student wants to compare the size of the blue whale with the size of the largest known dinosaur. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4018.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived.
  • An adult blue whale can weigh about 150 metric tons.
  • The largest known dinosaur, Argentinosaurus, may have weighed about 70 metric tons.
  • Blue whales feed mainly on tiny shrimp-like animals called krill.
choices: The blue whale, which can weigh about 150 metric tons, is the largest animal known to have lived.
Blue whales, which can weigh about 150 metric tons, feed mainly on tiny shrimp-like animals called krill.
Argentinosaurus, the largest known dinosaur, may have weighed about 70 metric tons.
A blue whale, at about 150 metric tons, can weigh more than twice as much as Argentinosaurus (about 70 tons).
r4018.explain: A comparison needs both animals: D gives both weights and the relationship ("more than twice as much"). A implies a comparison without naming the dinosaur, B is about diet, and C gives only one side.

r4019.sub: Emphasize a limitation of a finding
r4019.stem: The student wants to point out a limitation of the study's findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4019.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A study tested a new app designed to reduce teenagers' screen time.
  • Participants who used the app reduced their screen time by 30 minutes a day on average.
  • The study lasted four weeks.
  • All participants were volunteers who said they wanted to cut back.
  • The researchers did not track participants after the study ended.
choices: Its participants were volunteers eager to cut back, followed for just four weeks, so the results may not generalize.
Teenage participants who used the app reduced their screen time by 30 minutes a day on average over four weeks.
The study, which lasted four weeks, tested a new app designed to help teenagers reduce their screen time.
The researchers recruited volunteers who wanted to cut back on screen time and tested the app for four weeks.
r4019.explain: A limitation is a reason to be cautious about the results. A uses two notes (self-selected volunteers, a short study without follow-up) to explain why. B reports the result itself.

r4020.sub: Specify a place and a purpose
r4020.stem: The student wants to describe where the Great Green Wall is and what it is meant to do. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4020.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The Great Green Wall is a project in Africa.
  • It aims to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land.
  • It stretches across the Sahel, the region south of the Sahara.
  • The goal is to slow desertification and support farming communities.
  • Progress has varied widely from country to country.
choices: Progress on the Great Green Wall has varied widely from one participating country to another.
The Great Green Wall aims to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land to support farming communities.
Spanning Africa's Sahel, the Great Green Wall aims to restore degraded land and slow desertification.
The Sahel, the region south of the Sahara, is the site of a project that has made uneven progress.
r4020.explain: The goal has two parts: location and purpose. C gives both. B gives a target without the location, and D gives a location without the project.

r4021.sub: A comparison favoring one option for a stated reason
r4021.stem: The student wants to argue that heat pumps use energy more efficiently than gas furnaces. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4021.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Heat pumps and gas furnaces can both heat homes.
  • A heat pump moves heat from outside air into a home; a furnace burns fuel to create heat.
  • Heat pumps can deliver about three units of heat for each unit of electricity they use.
  • Furnaces deliver slightly less than one unit of heat for each unit of fuel energy.
  • Heat pumps cost more to install.
choices: A heat pump delivers about three units of heat per unit of electricity; a furnace, under one per unit of fuel.
Heat pumps cost more to install than gas furnaces, though both can heat homes effectively in most climates.
Both heat pumps and gas furnaces can heat homes, but heat pumps move heat while furnaces create it.
A heat pump moves heat from the outside air into a home, while a furnace burns fuel to create heat.
r4021.explain: Efficiency means heat delivered per unit of energy used. A compares exactly that. D explains how each works but makes no efficiency claim, and B works against the argument.

r4022.stem: The student wants to present the experiment's results as evidence against a common assumption. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4022.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • People often assume that more choices make shoppers happier.
  • In one experiment, a store offered either 6 or 24 varieties of jam for tasting.
  • The 24-variety display attracted more visitors.
  • But 30% of visitors to the 6-variety display bought jam, compared with 3% at the 24-variety display.
choices: The display with 24 varieties of jam attracted more visitors than the display with 6, as the assumption predicts.
A store tested the common assumption about choice by offering either 6 or 24 varieties of jam for tasting.
Despite the belief that more choice pleases shoppers, those offered 6 jams were ten times as likely to buy.
Shoppers offered 24 varieties of jam bought 3% of the time, while the larger display drew more visitors.
r4022.explain: The goal requires naming the assumption and showing results that cut against it. C does both: 30% versus 3% is ten times as likely. A reports a result that seems to fit the assumption, B describes only the method, and D gives figures from the notes without naming the assumption or making the comparison that undercuts it.

r4023.stem: The student wants to explain why helium has its name. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4023.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The element helium was first detected in the Sun.
  • In 1868, astronomers saw an unexpected yellow line in sunlight passing through a prism.
  • The line did not match any known element.
  • Helium is named after Helios, the Greek god of the Sun.
  • Helium was found on Earth in 1895.
choices: Helium was first detected in sunlight in 1868 and was found on Earth in 1895, nearly thirty years later.
In 1868, astronomers saw an unexpected yellow line in sunlight that did not match any known element.
Helium, which was found on Earth in 1895, is named after Helios, a figure from Greek mythology.
Because helium was first detected in the Sun, it was named after Helios, the Greek god of the Sun.
r4023.explain: An explanation of the name needs the namesake (Helios) and the reason (first detected in the Sun). Only D links the two.

r4024.stem: The student wants to clarify the difference between weather and climate using an example. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4024.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Weather describes atmospheric conditions over hours or days.
  • Climate describes average conditions over decades.
  • A single cold winter is an example of weather.
  • A thirty-year rise in average winter temperature is an example of climate change.
  • Both weather and climate include temperature and precipitation.
choices: Both weather and climate describe temperature and precipitation, whether over hours, days, or decades.
Weather covers hours or days, like one cold winter; climate covers decades, like a thirty-year warming.
A single cold winter and a thirty-year rise in winter temperatures are both related to Earth's climate.
Climate describes average conditions over decades, such as a thirty-year rise in average winter temperature.
r4024.explain: The goal is a difference, with an example. B contrasts the time scales and gives an example of each. A and C describe similarities or connections, and D defines only one term.

r4025.sub: Emphasize the purpose of a design feature
r4025.stem: The student wants to explain the purpose of the steel sphere in Taipei 101. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
r4025.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The Taipei 101 skyscraper in Taiwan is 508 meters tall.
  • A 660-metric-ton steel sphere hangs near the top of the building.
  • The sphere is a "tuned mass damper."
  • It sways opposite to the building's motion, reducing swaying during strong winds and earthquakes.
  • Visitors can view the sphere from an observation deck.
choices: Visitors to the 508-meter Taipei 101 can view its 660-metric-ton steel sphere from an observation deck.
Taipei 101, a 508-meter skyscraper in Taiwan, has a 660-metric-ton steel sphere hanging near its top.
The steel sphere hanging near the top of Taipei 101 is a 660-metric-ton device called a tuned mass damper.
The sphere in Taipei 101 sways opposite to the building, reducing its sway in strong winds and earthquakes.
r4025.explain: Purpose means what the sphere does for the building. D explains that it counteracts the building's sway. C names the device without saying what it does, and A describes it as a sight for visitors.

r4026.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4026.passage: Early in her career, the photographer Imogen Hart was told that portraits of factory workers would never sell. She resolved to prove her critics wrong. although she had little money, she spent three years photographing mill workers in their homes and at their machines, then exhibited the portraits in a gallery known for showing paintings by famous artists.
choices: Nevertheless,
In contrast,
Even so,
To that end,
r4026.explain: The sentence describes the steps Hart took to reach the goal stated just before ("prove her critics wrong"), so "To that end" fits. The contrast ("although she had little money") is already handled inside the sentence. Trap: three choices signal contrast, but the relationship to the previous sentence is purpose.

r4027.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4027.passage: Critics of electric cars point out that producing their batteries generates more carbon emissions than building a gasoline engine. studies that account for a car's full lifetime find that an electric car typically makes up for that difference within two years of driving, because charging it produces fewer emissions than burning gasoline.
choices: Granted,
Still,
Similarly,
For example,
r4027.explain: The first sentence states a critics' point; the second says that point doesn't settle the matter. "Still" signals that the conclusion holds despite what was just said. "Granted" (A) would introduce a concession, but the second sentence is the rebuttal, not the concession.

r4028.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4028.passage: The last known Tasmanian tiger, or thylacine, died in a zoo in 1936, but some residents of Tasmania insist that they have glimpsed the animal in the wild. more than a thousand reported sightings have been logged since the 1930s, although none has been confirmed with clear photographs or physical evidence.
choices: However,
Instead,
In fact,
As a result,
r4028.explain: The second sentence intensifies the first: not just "some residents" but more than a thousand reported sightings. "In fact" introduces a stronger version of the previous point. The "although" clause supplies its own contrast, so "However" (A) isn't needed.

r4029.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4029.passage: Bamboo can grow as much as 90 centimeters in a single day, and many species reach full height in just a few months. bamboo forests that are harvested can regenerate far more quickly than forests of slow-growing hardwood trees.
choices: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Previously,
By contrast,
r4029.explain: Fast regrowth is the cause, and quick regeneration after harvest is the result: "Consequently." "By contrast" (D) mislabels the relationship; the comparison with hardwoods is inside the second sentence, not between the sentences.

r4030.sub: A specific instance of a general claim
r4030.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4030.passage: Many traditional building methods are surprisingly well suited to hot climates. the wind towers of Yazd, Iran, catch breezes high above the city and funnel them down into homes, cooling rooms without electricity.
choices: For instance,
Moreover,
In conclusion,
Even so,
r4030.explain: The wind towers are one example of a traditional method suited to heat. "Moreover" (B) would add a separate point, but this sentence illustrates the first one.

r4031.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4031.passage: The town's population has not so much declined as aged. the number of residents has barely changed since 1990, but the share of residents over sixty-five has doubled while the number of school-age children has fallen by half.
choices: Moreover,
Nevertheless,
Specifically,
However,
r4031.explain: The second sentence gives the precise details behind "aged rather than declined": steady numbers, a doubled share of older residents, half as many children. "Specifically" introduces exact details of the general claim. "Moreover" (A) would add a new point rather than spell out this one, and nothing is contrasted.

r4032.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4032.passage: Honeybees are often celebrated as the world's most important pollinators. many crops, including tomatoes and blueberries, are pollinated more effectively by wild bees such as bumblebees, which can vibrate flowers to release pollen.
choices: Similarly,
Thus,
Specifically,
Yet
r4032.explain: The second sentence qualifies the celebration of honeybees by pointing out crops that wild bees pollinate better. "Yet" signals that contrast. "Thus" (B) would wrongly make the second point follow from the first.

r4033.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
r4033.passage: In 1912, the passenger ship Titanic sank after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic. in 1914, thirteen nations signed the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, requiring enough lifeboats for everyone on board.
choices: Previously,
Subsequently,
Meanwhile,
Likewise,
r4033.explain: The convention came after the sinking (1914 follows 1912), so "Subsequently" fits. "Previously" (A) reverses the order, and "Meanwhile" (C) implies the events happened at the same time.

r4034.sub: Similar case in a different field
r4034.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
